samples.summary: "still ticks a rapid second click on the checkbox itself" only asserts `toggles.length` — the untick it exists to protect is unasserted
samples.evidence: The test dispatches two clicks (detail 1 then 2) on the checkbox and asserts only `expect(toggles.length).toBe(2)`. The comment says the point is that "dropping it would swallow the untick", but the reported `checked` values are never inspected. A regression that reported `[[0,true],[0,true]]` (never producing the untick — plausible since `preventDefault()` reverts the DOM `checked` in jsdom before the second click) passes this test unchanged. Compare the sibling test at line ~93 which does assert `toEqual([[2,true],[3,false]])`.

samples.summary: The new `list`/`canIndent`/`canOutdent` fields of `computeActiveFormats` (what the toolbar reads) are never asserted
samples.evidence: commands.test.ts asserts only `.bold`, `.italic`, `.link` of `computeActiveFormats` (lines 56-78). `computeListState` is tested directly in list-commands.test.ts, but the pass-through added in `computeActiveFormats` — the only thing the toolbar consumes — has no test; swapping `canIndent`/`canOutdent` or dropping `list` would go unnoticed by the notes suite.

samples.summary: New toolbar list group (5 controls, pressed/disabled states) has no test anywhere in the frontend suite
samples.evidence: There is no notes-toolbar test file: packages/frontend/src/app/notes/ contains only yorkie-note-store.test.ts and notes-undo-integration.test.ts, and grepping `notes-toolbar`/`Bullet list`/`Indent` under packages/frontend/tests returns no notes matches. So the wiring of the three toggles to `editor.toggleBulletList/OrderedList/TaskList`, the `pressed={formats.list === ...}` mapping, and the `disabled={!formats.canIndent/canOutdent}` gating are untested (including the new EMPTY_FORMATS defaults). Same gap as pre-existing toolbar buttons, hence minor.

samples.summary: The "one transaction / one undo unit" claims for list toggles and for the checkbox rewrite are not tested
samples.evidence: `replacePrefixes` documents "as one transaction so the whole block is a single undo unit" and checkbox-input.ts documents "one undo unit and one store edit rather than an insert followed by a correction". Neither test file exercises undo: list-commands.test.ts and checkbox-input.test.ts only assert resulting doc text and selection; no `undo()` from @codemirror/commands and no transaction-count assertion appear in either. A refactor into per-line dispatches would keep every existing assertion green.
searchedFor: read list-commands.test.ts and checkbox-input.test.ts in full

samples.summary: A click on a nested *task* child (rather than a plain bullet child) is untested, so the line mapped for nested tasks is unverified
samples.evidence: preview.test.ts covers a plain nested `li` under a task ("leaves a plain nested item under a task to that item") but never renders nested task items (`- [ ] parent\n  - [ ] child`) and clicks the child. That is the case where `clickedItem === item` holds for the child and `data-source-line` from the core rule must resolve to the child's own line; an off-by-one or ancestor mix-up there would flip the parent and no test would fail.
searchedFor: grep for nested task fixtures ('- [ ] parent') in preview.test.ts
read the note-task-source-line core rule in preview.ts

samples.summary: `LIST_RE`'s alternative markers (`*`, `+`, `1)`) and multi-range (multi-cursor) selections are never exercised
samples.evidence: Every fixture in list-commands.test.ts uses `-` or `1.` markers and a single selection range. `kindOf` classifies `*`/`+` as bullet and `1)` as ordered, and all commands operate on `state.selection.main` only — none of that is asserted.

samples.summary: checkbox-input tests only type at end of line; a caret mid-line / trailing text after the box is untested
samples.evidence: `mount(doc, at = doc.length)` is always called without `at` except for the read-only variants, so `line.text.slice(0, from - line.from)` is always the whole line. The case `[ ]| trailing` (caret right after the box with text following) — where the slice matters and `to` is the caret rather than line end — has no test.

samples.summary: "does not claim a task click without a callback" is near-tautological on its defaultPrevented assertion
samples.evidence: With no `onToggleTask`, `onTaskClick` is never attached, so `expect(event.defaultPrevented).toBe(false)` holds for reasons unrelated to any logic in the handler; only the `note-tasks-interactive` class assertion carries information. Harmless, but it reads as coverage of the no-callback path that it does not provide.

finding.summary: Test titled "numbers an ordered list per indent level" uses a fixture with no indent levels, so the per-level counter logic is untested
finding.evidence:
The test at list-commands.test.ts:57-63 mounts `'a
b
c'` — three lines all at indent 0 — and asserts `'1. a
2. b
3. c'`. The behavior it claims to cover is `toggleKind`'s `counters = new Map<number, number>()` keyed by `p.indent.length` (list-commands.ts:222,231-232). With a flat fixture the map only ever has key `0`, so replacing the whole Map with a single `let n = 0` counter would leave this test green. No other test in the file toggles an ordered list over a nested/multi-indent selection (I grepped the file for `toggleOrderedList` — only two uses: this test and none with indentation; the indent/outdent block only uses bullets and a pre-existing `1. a
2. b`). The per-indent-level restart is new behavior shipped with a test that is presented as its coverage but cannot fail on it.

verdict.reason:
The finding's quoted evidence does not match the repository. The test "numbers an ordered list per indent level" (list-commands.test.ts:68-77) does NOT mount a flat 'a
b
c'; it mounts 'a
  b
  c
d' — two distinct indent levels (0 and 2) — selects all four lines, and asserts '1. a
  1. b
  2. c
2. d'. That fixture directly exercises the counters Map keyed by p.indent.length (list-commands.ts:233, 242-243): the nested child list restarts at 1, and the parent level resumes at 2 across it. The finding's own hypothesized mutation (replacing the Map with a single `let n = 0`) would produce '1. a
  2. b
  3. c
4. d' and fail the assertion, so the test is not vacuous and the per-level restart is not untested. The in-test comment states this rationale explicitly. Glob '**/list-commands*.ts' shows only one source and one test file, so there is no alternate/stale copy matching the reviewer's quote. The secondary claim that no toggleOrderedList use involves indentation is also false for this use.
